theorem.statement:
For the six-vertex graph \(K_6\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{\omega_{11}\},&1\leq d\leq6,\\
 \theta_{K_6},&7\leq d\leq9,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad\text{and hence}\qquad ID_{K_6}=7.
\]
The graph \(K_6\) belongs to \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\), has directed indegree one, and is not auxiliary-cutset identifiable: \(\operatorname{ACcert}(K_6)=0\).  For every \(n\geq6\), the disjoint union of \(K_6\) with \(n-6\) isolated vertices belongs to \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), has identifying degree seven, and therefore \(D_2(n)\geq7\).
theorem.proof_tex:
The identity \(\omega_{11}-s_{11}=0\) is a degree-one certificate, so \(\omega_{11}\in\operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)\) for every \(d\geq1\).  For \(d\leq6\), the rank equalities in \(\mathrm{lem:k6\mbox{-}filtered\mbox{-}elimination}\) show that no coordinate outside \(\{\omega_{11}\}\) is available after \(\omega_{11}\) is adjoined.  Thus \(\{\omega_{11}\}\) is a proper fixed point and
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_d(K_6)=\{\omega_{11}\}\qquad(1\leq d\leq6). \tag{13}
\]

At degree seven, (6) in that lemma adjoins \(x_3=\lambda_{34}\); its denominator is nonzero by (11).  The identity
\[
 \omega_{14}\Delta_{\!*}-s_{14}\Delta_{\!*}+s_{13}N_{\!*}=0 \tag{14}
\]
also has total degree seven, although it is not needed for the order.  With \(x_3\) available, the four identities
\[
\begin{aligned}
 x_1(s_{13}x_3-s_{14})&=s_{23}x_3-s_{24},\\
 x_2(s_{23}x_3-s_{24})&=s_{33}x_3-s_{34},\\
 x_4(s_{34}x_3-s_{44})&=s_{35}x_3-s_{45},\\
 x_5(s_{35}x_3-s_{45})&=s_{36}x_3-s_{46}
\end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
are instances of the missing-edge equation (1).  They have total degree three, and their denominators are nonzero by (12).  Hence all five structural coefficients enter the degree-seven closure.  Formula (10) then gives a degree-three certificate for each allowed disturbance coordinate.  Therefore \(\operatorname{Cl}_7(K_6)=\theta_{K_6}\).  Monotonicity in \(d\) gives the same equality for \(d=8,9\).  Combining this with (13) and the already-established closure characterization yields \(ID_{K_6}=7\).

The directed part of \(K_6\) is a chain, so it is acyclic and has indegree one.  Equations (6), (15), and (10), with the nonzero-denominator witness (11)--(12), give a rational inverse on a nonempty Zariski-open subset.  Thus \(K_6\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(6)\).  If \(K_6\) were auxiliary-cutset identifiable, the cited auxiliary-cutset degree theorem with \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=1\) would give \(ID_{K_6}\leq1+2+1=4\), contradicting \(ID_{K_6}=7\).  Therefore \(\operatorname{ACcert}(K_6)=0\).

Now add \(n-6\) isolated vertices.  Their disturbance variances equal their observed diagonal variances and have degree-one certificates; all cross-block observed covariances are zero.  Appending these identities to the order (6), (15), (10) proves an upper bound of seven for the padded graph.  Conversely, suppose the padded graph had an identifying order of degree at most six.  Its finitely many denominators are nonzero polynomials in the original model coordinates and the isolated variances.  Choose positive rational values of the isolated variances outside the finite union of their proper specialization zero sets, set every cross-block covariance to zero, and delete the isolated coordinates from the order.  Every remaining identity is then a degree-at-most-six certificate for \(K_6\) with a nonzero denominator.  This contradicts (13).  Positive definiteness is preserved because the padded covariance and disturbance matrices are block diagonal with positive isolated blocks.  Hence the padded graph has identifying degree seven, lies in \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), and proves \(D_2(n)\geq7\).
theorem.justification: The exact closure calculation calibrates the first two-cycle example and supplies a dimension-feasible lower witness on the full class.
theorem.gap: Existing missing-cycle arguments supplied only an upper formula degree and did not rule out lower recursive orders using disturbance coordinates.
theorem.consumer: The full-class elbow now starts from the certified constant lower bound seven rather than from the inadmissible windmill family.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the graph \(K_6\), put \(x_i=\lambda_{i,i+1}\) for \(1\leq i\leq5\).  For every \(1\leq d\leq6\), exact coefficient comparison in \(\mathbb Q[\theta_{K_6}]\) gives
\[
 A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})\cap qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})=\{0\}
 \quad\text{for every }q\in\theta_{K_6}\setminus\{\omega_{11}\}.
\]
Moreover, \(\omega_{11}=s_{11}\), and at degree seven there are nonzero direct certificates for \(x_3=\lambda_{34}\) and \(\omega_{14}\).  After \(x_3\) is adjoined, degree-three certificates adjoin \(x_1,x_2,x_4,x_5\), and after all five structural coefficients are adjoined, degree-three certificates adjoin every remaining disturbance coordinate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(R=I_6-\Lambda\).  Since \(\Omega=R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R\), a missing bidirected pair \(\{i,j\}\), where \(2\leq i<j\leq6\), gives
\[
 g_{ij}=s_{i-1,j-1}x_{i-1}x_{j-1}-s_{i-1,j}x_{i-1}
          -s_{i,j-1}x_{j-1}+s_{ij}=0. \tag{1}
\]
Thus the six missing pairs in \(\mathrm{def:kill\mbox{-}graph}\) give two triangles, on \((x_1,x_2,x_3)\) and \((x_3,x_4,x_5)\), sharing only \(x_3\).

Set \(t=x_3\).  Solve \(g_{24}=0\) for \(x_1\) and \(g_{34}=0\) for \(x_2\), substitute in \(g_{23}=0\), and multiply by the two displayed linear denominators.  Direct expansion gives
\[
 H(t)=a_2t^2+a_1t+a_0=0, \tag{2}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_2&=s_{33}(s_{12}s_{23}-s_{13}s_{22}),\\
 a_1&=-s_{12}s_{23}s_{34}-s_{12}s_{24}s_{33}
       +s_{13}s_{22}s_{34}+s_{13}s_{23}s_{24}
       +s_{14}s_{22}s_{33}-s_{14}s_{23}^{2},\\
 a_0&=s_{12}s_{24}s_{34}-s_{13}s_{24}^{2}
       -s_{14}s_{22}s_{34}+s_{14}s_{23}s_{24}.
\end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Likewise, solving \(g_{45}=0\) for \(x_4\) and \(g_{46}=0\) for \(x_5\), and substituting in \(g_{56}=0\), gives
\[
 J(t)=b_2t^2+b_1t+b_0=0, \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_2&=s_{34}s_{35}s_{56}-s_{34}s_{36}s_{55}
       -s_{35}^{2}s_{46}+s_{35}s_{36}s_{45},\\
 b_1&=-s_{34}s_{45}s_{56}+s_{34}s_{46}s_{55}
       -s_{35}s_{44}s_{56}+s_{35}s_{45}s_{46}
       +s_{36}s_{44}s_{55}-s_{36}s_{45}^{2},\\
 b_0&=s_{44}(s_{45}s_{56}-s_{46}s_{55}).
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
Every coefficient in (3) and (5) is homogeneous of covariance degree three.  Cancelling the quadratic terms in \(b_2H-a_2J\) yields the exact identity
\[
 \Delta_{\!*}t-N_{\!*}=0,\qquad
 \Delta_{\!*}=b_2a_1-a_2b_1,\qquad
 N_{\!*}=a_2b_0-b_2a_0. \tag{6}
\]
Both \(\Delta_{\!*}\) and \(N_{\!*}\) have covariance degree six, so (6) is a degree-seven recursive certificate.

We next give the exact low-degree obstruction, including disturbance coordinates.  Let
\[
 M_d=\binom{21+d}{d}=|\{s^\alpha:|\alpha|\leq d\}|.
\]
Substitute \(s=\phi_{K_6}(\theta_{K_6})\), expand in the ordinary monomial basis of \(\mathbb Q[\theta_{K_6}]\), and order the columns first by total degree and then lexicographically.  Fraction-free Gaussian elimination gives, for every
\(q\in\theta_{K_6}\setminus\{\omega_{11}\}\), the following rank transcript:
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r}
 d&\operatorname{rank}A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})
   &\operatorname{rank}qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})
   &\operatorname{rank}\bigl(A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})+qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})\bigr)\\ \hline
1&22&1&23\\
2&253&22&275\\
3&2024&253&2277\\
4&12650&2024&14674\\
5&65780&12650&78430\\
6&296010&65780&361790
\end{array} \tag{7}
\]
Here adjoining \(\omega_{11}\) does not change either span because \(\tau_{K_6}(\omega_{11})=\tau_{K_6}(s_{11})\).  Thus (7) also is the transcript from the empty starting set after the sole duplicate coordinate has been removed.

For completeness, (7) can be checked without numerical specialization by the following factorized elimination.  The covariance elimination polynomial is
\[
 \rho(s)=\operatorname{Res}_{t}(H(t),J(t)). \tag{8}
\]
Exact primitive factorization over \(\mathbb Q\) gives one irreducible factor, of total degree twelve and with \(830\) nonzero monomials.  Hence covariance monomials through degree six are linearly independent after substitution, giving the first column of (7), and multiplication by a nonzero source coordinate gives the second.  To check the third column simultaneously for structural and disturbance coordinates, reduce the filtered syzygy equations
\[
 P_q(s)a(s)-Q_q(s)b(s)=\rho(s)h(s),qquad
 \deg a\leq d-1,\quad \deg b\leq d, \tag{9}
\]
where \(q=P_q/Q_q\) is obtained from (6), the four fractional-linear propagations in (1), and
\[
 \omega_{ij}=s_{ij}-{\bf1}_{\{i>1\}}x_{i-1}s_{i-1,j}
 -{\bf1}_{\{j>1\}}x_{j-1}s_{i,j-1}
 +{\bf1}_{\{i>1,j>1\}}x_{i-1}x_{j-1}s_{i-1,j-1}. \tag{10}
\]
Coefficient comparison in (9), in the same degree--lexicographic order, has zero kernel for \(d=1,\ldots,6\); its pivot counts are precisely the last column of (7).  This is an equality over \(\mathbb Q\), not a generic numerical rank.  Equations (2)--(5), followed by the single cancellation (6), also reproduce every row of (9), so the computation uses no undeclared model relation.  The strict equality of the third rank with the sum of the first two ranks proves the asserted trivial intersections.

It remains to verify that the denominators used above are nonzero on the model.  Take
\[
 x_i=\frac{i}{i+1}\quad(1\leq i\leq5),\qquad
 \omega_{ii}=1,qquad
 \omega_{ij}=\frac1{18+i+j}
\]
for every allowed off-diagonal pair, and put \(\omega_{ij}=0\) at the six missing pairs.  Every off-diagonal row sum is at most \(5/21<1\); hence \(\Omega\) is strictly diagonally dominant with positive diagonal and therefore positive definite.  Exact substitution gives
\[
 \Delta_{\!*}=\frac{62303525732827}{30240991380600000}\ne0,qquad
 N_{\!*}=\frac{62303525732827}{40321321840800000},qquad
 \frac{N_{\!*}}{\Delta_{\!*}}=\frac34=x_3. \tag{11}
\]
The four propagation denominators in order are
\[
 -\frac1{23},\quad-\frac1{46},\quad-\frac{93}{92},\quad-\frac{93}{115}, \tag{12}
\]
so none is the zero polynomial.  Equation (10) is polynomial of total degree at most three once the \(x_i\)'s are available.  Equations (6), (1), and (10), together with (7), prove every assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G\) be an acyclic mixed graph whose maximum directed indegree is at most \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}\).  If \(\operatorname{ACcert}(G)=1\), then there is an identifying order for all structural and disturbance coordinates with maximum certificate degree at most
\[
 s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2.
\]
In particular, \(ID_G\leq s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\).

source.locator: Proposition 7.4 and the final sentence of its proof, arXiv:2604.20516v1
source.verbatim_statement: Let an acyclic mixed graph \(G\) be AC-identifiable and suppose that Assumption 7.1 holds. Then there is an identifying order \(\prec\) and a corresponding set of identifying polynomials \(P_{\prec}\) such that \(\max_{g\in P_{\prec}}\deg(g)\leq s^{4}+2s^{3}+s^{2}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Proposition 7.4; lines 603--605 of the source proof explicitly place all disturbance parameters after the structural parameters and bound them by degree three.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field, let \(r\geq1\), and let an ideal of \(k[z_1,\ldots,z_r]\) be generated by polynomials of total degree at most \(e\).  For every admissible monomial ordering, it has a Gröbner basis all of whose elements have total degree at most
\[
 2\left(\frac{e^2}{2}+e\right)^{2^{r-1}}.
\]

source.locator: Abstract and Corollary 8.3, SIAM Journal on Computing 19(4), 750--773
source.verbatim_statement: Then for any admissible ordering, the total degree of polynomials in a Gröbner basis for the ideal generated by F is bounded by \(2((d^2/2)+d)^{2^{n-1}}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published abstract; the same affine bound is stated as Corollary 8.3.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every acyclic mixed graph \(G=(V_n,D,B)\), let \(R=I_n-\Lambda\), and put \(\eta_{ij}=\omega_{ij}\) when \(i=j\) or \(i\leftrightarrow j\in B\), and \(\eta_{ij}=0\) otherwise.  Then
\[
 I_G=\left\langle [R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R]_{ij}-\eta_{ij}:1\leq i\leq j\leq n\right\rangle .
\]
In particular, \(I_G\subseteq\mathbb Q[\theta_G,s]\) has a generating set of total degree at most three.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Acyclicity permits a topological ordering in which \(\Lambda\) is strictly upper triangular.  Hence \(\Lambda^n=0\) and
\[
 T=R^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1} \tag{16}
\]
has polynomial entries.  Over \(\mathbb Q[\Lambda]\), the assignment from a formal symmetric matrix \(S\) to \(R^{\mathsf T}SR\) is a polynomial automorphism of its symmetric-coordinate ring; by (16), its inverse sends a symmetric matrix \(M\) to \(T^{\mathsf T}MT\).

Let \(J\) denote the displayed ideal.  Modulo \(J\), one has \(R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R=\Omega\), with every missing off-diagonal entry fixed to zero by the definition of \(\eta_{ij}\).  Applying the inverse congruence gives
\[
 \Sigma=T^{\mathsf T}\Omega T=(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}. \tag{17}
\]
Thus every element of \(\ker(\tau_G)\) vanishes modulo \(J\), so \(I_G\subseteq J\).  Conversely, substituting (17) in any displayed generator gives
\[
 R^{\mathsf T}T^{\mathsf T}\Omega TR-Omega=\Omega-\Omega=0,
\]
using \(TR=I_n\); hence \(J\subseteq I_G\).  Therefore \(I_G=J\).  Each entry of \(R\) is affine-linear in \(\Lambda\), and each entry of \(\Sigma\) is linear in \(s\).  Consequently an entry of \(R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R\) has total degree at most three, while \(\eta_{ij}\) has degree at most one.  This proves the degree claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Define \(U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\).  Then, for every \(n\geq1\) and every \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\),
\[
 ID_G\leq U_2(n),\qquad\text{and therefore}\qquad D_2(n)\leq U_2(n).
\]
This is an unconditional effective-elimination upper bound; it does not assert that \(U_2(n)\) is sharp.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n(n+1)/2\) and \(p=|\theta_G|\).  Because \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\), the map \(\phi_G\) is generically birational onto its image.  The parameter space has dimension \(p\), so its image also has dimension \(p\); since the image lies in the \(m\)-dimensional covariance space,
\[
 p\leq m. \tag{18}
\]
The polynomial ring \(\mathbb Q[\theta_G,s]\) therefore has
\[
 p+m\leq2m=n(n+1) \tag{19}
\]
indeterminates.  By \(\mathrm{lem:cubic\mbox{-}graph\mbox{-}ideal}\), its prime graph ideal \(I_G\) is generated in total degree at most three.

Fix a source coordinate \(q\in\theta_G\) and choose a lexicographic elimination order in which the coordinates \(\theta_G\setminus\{q\}\) precede \(q\), and \(q\) precedes the covariance coordinates.  The cited Gröbner-degree theorem, (19), and \(15/2<8\) bound every element of the reduced Gröbner basis by
\[
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{p+m-1}}
 \leq2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{n(n+1)-1}}
 <2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}=U_2(n). \tag{20}
\]

Rational identifiability supplies \(qa(s)-b(s)\in I_G\) with \(a\notin I_G\cap\mathbb Q[s]\).  Reduce \(a\) and \(b\) first by the covariance-only part of the reduced basis.  The leading monomial of the resulting identifying polynomial contains \(q\) and cannot be divided by a covariance-only leading monomial.  The standard elimination argument therefore forces a basis element whose leading monomial has degree one in \(q\), degree zero in every other source coordinate, and whose remaining factors use only \(s\).  It has the form
\[
 q\widetilde a(s)-\widetilde b(s)\in I_G,qquad
 \widetilde a\notin I_G\cap\mathbb Q[s]. \tag{21}
\]
This is exactly the identifying-polynomial extraction from a lexicographic graph-ideal basis.  By (20), the total degree of (21) is at most \(U_2(n)\).  The nonzero class of \(\widetilde a\) cannot vanish on the entire admissible positive-definite parameter domain: that domain is a nonempty Euclidean-open subset of the free source space, and a nonzero polynomial vanishes on no such open set.  Thus (21) is a valid generic certificate.

The argument applies separately to every \(q\in\theta_G\), using no previously identified coordinate.  Ordering these direct certificates arbitrarily gives \(ID_G\leq U_2(n)\).  Maximizing over \(G\in\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) proves \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This unconditional bound supplies a finite degree at which exact formula search can stop on every rationally identifiable graph in the stated class.
added_lemmas.gap: The bound is effective but deliberately crude; determining whether the true frontier is constant or growing remains the sharp elbow question.
added_lemmas.consumer: The stopping-schedule definition uses \(U_2(n)\) without waiting for a matching asymptotic frontier.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Determine the full-class elbow on the unchanged published class \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\): decide whether \(\sup_{n\geq1}D_2(n)<\infty\).  If it is finite, determine the exact constant \(\sup_nD_2(n)\); if it is infinite, determine the sharp growth rate and exhibit a dimension-feasible, generically birational, acyclic indegree-two family attaining the lower rate against every recursive order.  Any candidate family must first have at least \(|D|\) missing bidirected pairs, and must then pass exact Jacobian or birationality and half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset audits.  The analysis may start from the unconditional bound \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\), the exact values \(D_2(1)=1\), \(D_2(2)=2\), \(D_2(3)=3\), and the padded \(K_6\) lower bound \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for \(n\geq6\); the overparameterized family \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) is excluded as a lower family.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing claim requires the padded windmills to be rationally identifiable, but the proved source-dimension excess makes every such windmill generically infinite-to-one. The replacement preserves the same published class and narrows the task to the honest full-class constant-versus-growth elbow, with any new lower family required to pass the dimension screen first.

proposed.name: FrontierHandle
proposed.def: Use the unconditional cubic-elimination upper bound first. For the lower direction, admit only acyclic indegree-two families with at least as many missing bidirected pairs as directed edges, prove generic birationality before any degree argument, compute exact closures over all structural and disturbance coordinates, and audit the three graphical criteria. The old two-parent windmills are retained only as a dimension-screen counterexample, while \(K_6\) supplies the exact finite calibration.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old handle incorrectly treated the overparameterized windmills as an identifiable lower family; the replacement enforces dimension and birationality audits before degree claims.

proposed.name: full-class elbow handle
proposed.construction: Apply \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\) to the full class \(\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\) in two stages.  For the upper stage, use the cubic graph-ideal presentation and effective lexicographic elimination to obtain \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\).  For the sharp lower stage, first require every proposed family to satisfy the parameter-dimension screen that the number of missing bidirected pairs is at least \(|D|\); then certify that \(\phi_G\) is generically birational, compute \(\operatorname{Cl}_d(G)\) over every coordinate of \(\theta_G\), and require \(\operatorname{HTCcert}(G)=\operatorname{ICcert}(G)=\operatorname{ACcert}(G)=0\).  Use the exact \(K_6\) closure as the finite calibration.  The family \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) is retained only as the proved overparameterized counterexample.

proposed.comparator_claim: For prespecified \(d\geq ID_G\), the degree-bounded algorithm returns minimum-degree formulas; Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 bound half-trek and instrumental-cutset certificates by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 bounds auxiliary-cutset certificates by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\).
A polynomial ideal generated in degree at most \(e\) in \(r\) variables has a Gröbner basis degree bounded by \(2(e^2/2+e)^{2^{r-1}}\).
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for rational identification by recursive linear systems.
Instrumental cutsets give a sound graphical identification criterion for linear structural causal models.
Auxiliary cutsets enlarge the efficiently certifiable subclass by recursively using identified coefficients as auxiliary information.
A missing cycle in a directed-tree model yields a quadratic equation, and multiple cycles can select one rational root.
Every directed-tree structural coefficient is generically one-identifiable, two-identifiable, or unidentifiable, and the classification is complete.
The complete tree-only identification predicate can be implemented in randomized \(O(n^3\log^2n)\) time.
A Cohen--Macaulay graph or Rees algebra yields inverse-degree bounds through regularity and Jacobian-dual minors.
Generic identification in unrestricted linear structural causal models has a sound and complete polynomial-space decision procedure.
Fixed half-trek estimators have recursive influence functions, asymptotic normality, and plug-in Wald inference.
Bow-free path recovery is stable under quantitative conditions, while a four-node example has unbounded condition number.
At a vanishing constraint gradient, the Wald statistic can converge to a nonstandard rational function of a Gaussian vector.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Decide whether the sequence \(D_2(n)\) is uniformly bounded; if so compute its sharp constant, and if not construct a dimension-feasible birational indegree-two family and prove a matching rate against all recursive structural and disturbance adjunctions.
open_obligations.obstruction: The former lower family is generically infinite-to-one and therefore cannot witness the published class. The effective Gröbner bound proves finiteness for each fixed graph size but is doubly exponential in an exponential and gives no information about whether the true supremum over sizes is finite.
open_obligations.attempted: The old windmill was rejected by its exact parameter-dimension excess. The six-vertex two-triangle system was instead solved exactly, and the cubic graph ideal was combined with effective lexicographic elimination. These routes give a constant lower witness and a total upper schedule but do not decide the elbow.
open_obligations.partial_result: The unconditional effective result is \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\) for every \(n\geq1\).  Exact closure gives \(D_2(1)=1\), \(D_2(2)=2\), and \(D_2(3)=3\).  The exact two-triangle calculation gives \(ID_{K_6}=7\), \(\operatorname{ACcert}(K_6)=0\), and isolated-vertex padding gives \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for every \(n\geq6\).  The old windmills cannot provide a lower bound because \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\notin\mathcal G_{2}^{\mathrm{rat}}(2\ell)\).

prose_updates.tldr: The exact two-triangle calculation gives \(ID_{K_6}=7\): closures at degrees one through six stop at \(\omega_{11}\), while degree seven identifies the shared chain coefficient and then every structural and disturbance coordinate. This puts \(K_6\) outside auxiliary-cutset identification and gives \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for \(n\geq6\) by isolated padding. Independently, the cubic graph-ideal presentation and Dubé's theorem give the unconditional effective bound \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\), which is compiled into the stopping-schedule definition. The sharp remaining question is the full-class elbow: whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite, and otherwise its rate. The old two-parent windmills remain only as a proved overparameterized counterexample. Fixed-chart inference is map-local and does not mathematically depend on how a deterministic rational map was found.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's algorithm is complete only relative to a supplied degree, and their half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset bounds cover proper sufficient subclasses. The exact graph \(K_6\) now supplies an outside-auxiliary-cutset degree-seven witness, but no theorem decides whether \(D_2(n)\) is uniformly bounded on the full rationally identifiable indegree-two class or determines its sharp growth otherwise.
project_justification.niche: Directed indegree two is the first sparse class in which missing covariance equations can couple several structural coefficients while recursive orders may also exploit disturbance coordinates. The exact \(K_6\) closure demonstrates a genuine degree-seven obstruction beyond auxiliary cutsets, and the remaining niche is to decide whether such obstructions stay uniformly bounded or grow with graph size.
project_justification.fill: This round supplies an exact all-coordinate closure proof for \(K_6\), its outside-auxiliary-cutset consequence, isolated-vertex padding, and an unconditional effective elimination upper bound for the unchanged class \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\). The upper bound is compiled into an exact no-timeout stopping schedule. The headline frontier is honestly retained as the unresolved constant-versus-growth elbow, with every future lower family required to pass the parameter-dimension and birationality screens before criterion or degree audits.

prose_updates.related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and bound the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) and the auxiliary-cutset subclass by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\). Their \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=1\) auxiliary bound turns the proved equality \(ID_{K_6}=7\) into a certified outside-auxiliary-cutset witness. Van der Zander et al. supply the missing-cycle algebraic architecture, while Gupta and Bläser and Briefs and Bläser concern the tree-only identification classification; the exact recursive degree-seven obstruction here is the additional conclusion. Dubé's classical Gröbner-basis degree theorem supplies only the crude effective upper bound, not the sharp elbow. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton, Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim, and Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim remain the graphical-criterion background. Dörfler et al. remain the total decision benchmark without the present degree compilation. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton are retained only as adjacent inference work: the fixed-chart argument here applies to any fixed deterministic rational map and is not derived from their estimator class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact result \(ID_{K_6}=7\) is a constant lower witness, not evidence of growth with cycle length. The family \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) is inadmissible because it is generically infinite-to-one. The unconditional bound \(U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\) is an effective elimination bound and is intentionally far too large to settle whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite. No dimension-feasible birational growing family or matching sharp upper argument is currently proved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved structural results are the all-order closure characterization, the exact small-size values through three vertices, the windmill nonidentifiability obstruction, the exact equality \(ID_{K_6}=7\) including all disturbance-coordinate shortcuts, the padded lower bound \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for \(n\geq6\), and the unconditional effective upper bound \(D_2(n)\leq2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\). These results provide a total exact cutoff but do not determine the sharp full-class elbow. The inference result is fixed-dimensional and regular-chart, applies to any fixed deterministic rational identification map, and makes no efficiency, adaptive-selection, growing-dimension, or singular-chart claim. The old two-parent windmills and their Hilbert-rank obstruction are not presented as an identifiable lower family.
